Convex Group is a Bermuda-based specialty insurance and reinsurance group launched in 2019 with large private backing, notably from Onex and the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan. It writes property, casualty, marine, energy, aviation and specialty risks through Lloyd's and its own carriers, selling to corporate clients through brokers. Headquartered in Hamilton with major hubs in London and Europe, it has grown to several billion dollars of premiums. Privately held. B2B insurer with low consumer awareness, though it has used some sports and brand sponsorship in the insurance sector.

GlobalWafers is a Taiwanese manufacturer of silicon wafers, the base material for semiconductor chips, and one of the world's top three producers alongside Shin-Etsu and SUMCO. It supplies chipmakers such as TSMC and memory makers, with plants in Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Europe, the US (Texas) and elsewhere after acquiring Siltronic's rival MEMC and Topsil. Founded in 2011 as a spin-off of Sino-American Silicon Products and listed in Taipei (6488). B2B component supplier with almost no consumer brand awareness.

McLarens is a global loss adjusting and claims management firm for the insurance industry, handling property, casualty, marine and specialty claims for insurers and corporate clients. It operates through a network of offices in many countries, with a major US presence in Atlanta, and has expanded by acquisition under private equity ownership. Revenue comes from fees for claims handling and related services. B2B service provider with limited brand awareness among the general public.

Naftogaz of Ukraine is Ukraine's state-owned national oil and gas company, headquartered in Kyiv, covering gas and oil production, storage, trading, supply and, formerly, transit of Russian gas to Europe. It owns Ukrtransgaz storage assets and Ukrnafta stakes and is the largest company in the country, supplying households and industry. Wholly owned by the Ukrainian state, its operations and finances have been heavily affected by the war since 2022. Well known domestically; little international consumer brand presence.

Nanya Technology is a Taiwanese maker of DRAM memory chips, part of the Formosa Plastics Group, founded in 1995 and listed in Taipei (2408). It supplies standard, specialty and mobile DRAM to makers of PCs, servers, consumer electronics, networking and automotive equipment, operating fabs in New Taipei, Taiwan. Revenue comes from chip sales to electronics manufacturers worldwide. B2B component supplier with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

Oando is a Nigerian integrated energy company based in Lagos, with upstream oil and gas, midstream, gas and power and trading operations. Its upstream arm took over Eni's Nigerian onshore assets and it holds stakes in blocks in the Niger Delta. Formerly a fuel retail and marketing business, it sells to industry, power plants and traders. Listed on the Nigerian Exchange (OANDO) and Johannesburg. Known in Nigeria; little profile elsewhere, and a past Nigerian sports sponsor.

Playtika is a mobile games developer and publisher known for free-to-play social casino and casual titles such as Slotomania, Bingo Blitz, House of Fun, Caesars Slots and Board Kings, with players in many countries. It earns revenue from in-app purchases and advertising, with annual revenue near 2.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Herzliya, Israel, with studios worldwide, it has been controlled by a Chinese-led consortium since 2016 and listed on Nasdaq (PLTK) in 2021. Large reach among casual gamers, though the company brand itself is little known.

RenaissanceRe is a Bermuda-based reinsurance group focused on property catastrophe reinsurance, plus casualty and specialty lines, and it manages third-party capital vehicles such as Medici and DaVinci. Customers are insurers and brokers worldwide, with revenue from premiums and fees. Founded in 1993 and headquartered in Pembroke, Hamilton, it is listed on the NYSE (RNR), with a market value of roughly 12 billion dollars. B2B reinsurer with low consumer awareness.

Staatsolie is the state-owned oil company of Suriname, based in Paramaribo. It explores for and produces crude oil onshore, refines it at its Tout Lui Faut refinery, and sells fuels and power through subsidiaries including its gas station and electricity businesses. It is positioned to benefit from large offshore discoveries made by TotalEnergies and APA Corp. Wholly government owned and a major source of national revenue. Well known within Suriname, little profile abroad.

Uganda National Oil Company (UNOC) is Uganda's state-owned oil company, established in 2015 and based in Kampala. It manages the government's commercial interests in the country's oil sector, including stakes in the Lake Albert development with TotalEnergies and CNOOC, the East African Crude Oil Pipeline to Tanzania, and fuel import and storage through its marketing arm. Wholly government owned. Mainly a national energy actor with little consumer brand profile outside Uganda.

Warba Bank is a Kuwaiti Islamic bank that began operations in 2010, offering retail, corporate and investment banking under Sharia principles, including financing, deposit accounts and card services. Headquartered in Kuwait City, it serves customers in Kuwait through a branch and digital network and is listed on Boursa Kuwait. Founded by Kuwaiti shareholders and state-linked investors. Consumer-facing bank with regional awareness in Kuwait, little outside the Gulf.

Wolters Kluwer is a Dutch global information services and software company serving legal, tax, accounting, finance, audit, risk, compliance and healthcare professionals. Products include CCH tax software, UpToDate clinical decision support, Kluwer legal publications and Enablon compliance tools. It sells subscriptions and software to businesses, hospitals and professionals worldwide with roughly 6 billion euros of revenue and about 21,000 employees. Headquartered in Alphen aan den Rijn and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (WKL). B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Air Liquide is a French multinational and world leader in industrial gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and argon, selling to the steel, chemicals, electronics, food and healthcare industries, and operating home healthcare services. Founded in 1902 and headquartered in Paris, it has over 66,000 employees in about 60 countries and revenue above 27 billion euros. Listed on Euronext Paris (AI). It is a known sponsor in motorsport circles, but is mostly a B2B industrial brand with moderate public awareness.

Authentic Brands Group is a New York brand management and licensing company that buys consumer, sports and entertainment brands and licenses them to manufacturers and retailers. Its portfolio includes Reebok, Brooks Brothers, Sports Illustrated, Shaquille O'Neal, Marilyn Monroe, Elvis Presley, Juicy Couture, Ted Baker and Champion's apparel business. Revenue comes from royalties on over 30 billion dollars of retail sales. Founded in 2010 by Jamie Salter, privately held with investors including BlackRock and Brookfield. Portfolio brands are very visible even if the group is not.

Bain Capital Specialty Finance is a US business development company managed by Bain Capital Credit that lends mainly to middle-market companies through senior secured loans. It is externally managed, headquartered in Boston, and listed on the NYSE (BCSF) with a portfolio of roughly 2.5 billion dollars. Income comes from interest on loans to private companies, paid out as dividends to investors. Financial vehicle with no consumer brand profile.

Beacon Pointe is a US registered investment advisor and wealth management firm based in Newport Beach, California, serving high-net-worth individuals, families, foundations and retirement plans. It has grown through many acquisitions of advisory firms and is backed by private equity investors. It manages tens of billions of dollars in client assets across offices in the US. Private wealth manager with regional brand profile and limited national consumer awareness.

Cellnex Telecom is a Spanish wireless and broadcast tower infrastructure operator, the largest independent tower company in Europe. It owns and manages over 100,000 towers and sites in Spain, France, Italy, the UK, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Ireland and other countries, leasing capacity to mobile network operators and broadcasters. Created from Abertis Telecom, it was listed in Madrid in 2015 (CLNX) and has expanded through large acquisitions. B2B infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.

Chemours is a US chemical company spun out of DuPont in 2015, headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware. It makes titanium dioxide pigment (Ti-Pure), fluoroproducts and refrigerants (Opteon, Freon), Teflon-brand materials and Nafion membranes. Customers are makers of paints, plastics, air conditioning, semiconductors and electric vehicles. Listed on the NYSE (CC), with revenue around 6 billion dollars. Teflon is a household name, but the Chemours corporate brand is mainly B2B, and it has faced PFAS litigation.

China Hongqiao Group is a Chinese aluminium producer and the world's largest by output, based in Zouping, Shandong. It operates an integrated chain from alumina refining to primary aluminium smelting and sells semi-finished aluminium products to manufacturers, with a stake in Indonesian bauxite and alumina operations. It is a subsidiary of Weiqiao and listed in Hong Kong (1378). Commodity producer with little consumer brand awareness.

Commercial Credit Group Inc. is a US commercial equipment finance company based in Charlotte, North Carolina, listed in Crunchbase under financial services and related industries. The Crunchbase description presents it as a commercial equipment lender. No further products, customers, size or ownership details are supported by the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Dover Corporation is a US diversified industrial manufacturer headquartered in Downers Grove, Illinois, with five segments: engineered products, clean energy and fueling, imaging and identification, pumps and process solutions, and climate and sustainability technologies. Products include fuel dispensers (Wayne), fluid pumps, refrigeration cases, marking and coding equipment and vehicle service lifts. Customers are industrial, retail and energy businesses. Founded in 1955, listed on the NYSE (DOV), with revenue around 8 billion dollars. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

Essential Utilities is a US regulated water, wastewater and natural gas utility holding company based in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania. Its Aqua subsidiary serves water and wastewater customers in Pennsylvania, Ohio, North Carolina, Illinois, Texas and other states, and Peoples serves natural gas customers in Pennsylvania and Kentucky. It serves several million people and is listed on the NYSE (WTRG). Regional utility with regulated revenue; brand known locally but not a typical sponsor.

Everforth is a US technology and digital engineering company based in Glen Allen, Virginia. Crunchbase classes it under consulting and information technology and describes it as a technology and digital engineering firm. It likely sells IT and engineering services to business customers, but the input does not support specifics on customers, scale or ownership. Little public brand awareness is indicated. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

HR Path is a French human resources consulting and software company founded in 2001 in Paris. It helps large employers implement and run HR information systems, such as SAP SuccessFactors, Workday and Oracle, and offers payroll, HR outsourcing and consulting services. It operates across Europe, North America, Asia and Latin America with several thousand staff. It is privately owned with private equity backing. B2B services firm with limited public brand awareness.

Informa is a London-listed (LSE: INF) international events, academic publishing and intelligence group. Its businesses include Informa Markets (trade shows such as the Cannes Lions, Arab Health and Fi events), Informa Connect, Taylor & Francis academic publisher and Informa TechTarget digital content. It serves exhibitors, researchers and business professionals worldwide, earning revenue from exhibition sales, subscriptions and sponsorship. Revenue is around 4 billion pounds. B2B brand known to marketers and event sponsors, with little consumer profile.

Interparking is a Belgian-based parking operator that builds, owns and manages car parks in Europe, with sites in Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, Italy and other countries, often in city centres, airports and stations. It earns money from parking fees, subscriptions and concession contracts with cities and property owners. Based in Brussels and owned by investors including Ardian after changes of owner. Consumer-facing service, though with limited brand awareness.

Itron is a US technology company based in Liberty Lake, Washington that makes smart metering, grid-edge intelligence and software for electricity, gas and water utilities. Products include communication modules, meters and analytics for utilities and cities, with millions of devices deployed worldwide. Founded in 1977 and listed on Nasdaq (ITRI), with revenue near 2.4 billion dollars. B2B supplier with low consumer awareness.

Kawasaki Heavy Industries is a Japanese industrial conglomerate based in Kobe and Tokyo, making motorcycles (Kawasaki Ninja, Z series), jet skis, rolling stock, aerospace components, ships, gas turbines, robots and hydrogen equipment. It sells to consumers, railway operators, defence ministries and industry, with revenue near 2 trillion yen and tens of thousands of employees. Founded in 1896 and listed in Tokyo (7012). The Kawasaki motorcycle brand is very visible globally and has a heavy motorsport presence.

Landbay is a UK specialist buy-to-let mortgage lender founded in 2014 and based in London. It lends to landlords through brokers using technology to speed up applications and underwriting, funded through its own balance sheet and capital partners. Customers are private landlords and property investors. Backed by private shareholders. Niche financial brand known among mortgage brokers, with little general consumer awareness.

Odoo is a Belgian open-source business software company, based near Louvain-la-Neuve, offering an all-in-one suite of apps for accounting, CRM, sales, inventory, manufacturing, e-commerce, HR and website building. It sells to small and medium-sized firms worldwide, earning money from subscriptions for hosted editions and from partner services. Founded in 2005 as TinyERP, with several million users. Raised funding from General Atlantic and others. B2B software with growing brand awareness among businesses, and it has sponsored sports teams, including cycling.

Opifex Synergy is a US company based in Tampa, Florida that, per Crunchbase, provides equipment rental, including construction equipment. It is classified as a business development entity. Beyond that the input gives no specifics on customers, scale or ownership. Likely a B2B rental and services business with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

PureCycle Technologies is a US company based in Orlando, Florida that has licensed a solvent-based process from Procter & Gamble to turn waste polypropylene plastic into ultra-pure recycled resin. Its first commercial plant is in Ironton, Ohio, with further plants planned in the US, Europe and Asia, and it has agreements with consumer goods firms such as Procter & Gamble and Nestle. Listed on Nasdaq (PCT) after a 2021 SPAC merger. Early-stage B2B materials business with low consumer awareness.

RR Donnelley is a Chicago-based commercial printing and marketing services company that prints books, catalogs, labels, direct mail, packaging and financial documents, and offers supply chain and marketing support. Founded in 1864, it was listed on the NYSE (RRD) before being taken private by Chatham Asset Management in 2022 after years of restructuring. Customers are publishers, retailers, banks and consumer brands. B2B service business with moderate name recognition among marketers, little among consumers.

Seadrill is an offshore drilling contractor that owns and operates deepwater drillships, semi-submersibles and jack-ups, leasing them with crews to oil majors and national oil companies such as Petrobras, Equinor and Shell. Originally part of John Fredriksen's group, it went through Chapter 11 and re-emerged in 2022, and is listed on the NYSE (SDRL) and Oslo. Operations are global with a regional presence in Houston. B2B oilfield services with no consumer brand awareness.

SJ Semi (SJSemi) is a Chinese semiconductor packaging and foundry-services company based in Jiangyin, Jiangsu, and part of the JCET Group ecosystem, focused on middle-end-of-line wafer processing such as bumping, redistribution layers and wafer-level packaging for advanced chips. Customers are chip designers and foundries. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand awareness. Established in the 2010s as a Chinese integrated circuit packaging supplier.

Sompo Holdings is a Japanese insurance group listed in Tokyo (8630), providing property and casualty insurance, life insurance, nursing care and overseas insurance through units such as Sompo Japan and Sompo International. The input lists Singapore, but the parent is headquartered in Tokyo, with Singapore as an Asia hub. It serves consumers and corporations worldwide and owns Van Gogh's Sunflowers. Revenue is around 4 trillion yen. Well known in Japan and a sports sponsor there, with moderate awareness elsewhere.

Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing is a Chinese electronics manufacturer based in Suzhou, Jiangsu, making flexible printed circuits, precision components and related electronics for consumer electronics, such as Apple and other smartphone makers, through its Multi-Fineline Electronix subsidiary acquired in 2016. It also produces LED display modules and has expanded into automotive and new energy components. Listed on the Shenzhen exchange. B2B supplier with limited consumer brand awareness.

Teraco is South Africa's largest vendor-neutral data centre operator, based in Johannesburg with facilities in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban. It hosts the servers and interconnections of internet providers, cloud companies, banks and enterprises, and provides the landing point for subsea cables. Founded in 2008 and majority owned since 2021 by Digital Realty, with Berkshire Partners historically an investor. B2B infrastructure with little public brand awareness.

Northwestern Mutual is a US financial services mutual company headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, selling life, disability and long-term care insurance, annuities and investment advice through a large network of financial advisors. It is policyholder-owned, with millions of clients and well over 500 billion dollars in assets under management. Founded in 1857. It is a well-known US consumer brand that advertises heavily and sponsors sports and community events, including naming rights in Milwaukee.

Vishay Intertechnology is a US maker of discrete semiconductors, such as diodes and MOSFETs, and passive electronic components such as resistors, capacitors and inductors. Customers are automotive, industrial, computing, consumer, telecom and medical electronics makers, with manufacturing in Asia, Europe and the Americas. Based in Malvern, Pennsylvania, founded in 1962 and listed on the NYSE (VSH), with revenue around 3 billion dollars. B2B component supplier with no consumer profile.

Webuild is Italy's largest construction and engineering group, building large infrastructure such as railways, metros, dams, bridges, roads and airports in dozens of countries, including the Rome Metro, the Snowy 2.0 hydro project in Australia and the Salini Impregilo projects in Africa. Formerly Salini Impregilo, it was renamed Webuild in 2020 and is listed in Milan (WBD) with the Salini family and Cassa Depositi e Prestiti as shareholders. Revenue is above 10 billion euros. Known to governments and business, with modest consumer awareness.

Austin Powder is a US maker of industrial explosives and blasting systems, headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio and founded in 1833. It sells detonators, cast boosters and bulk explosives to mining, quarry and construction customers across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia. Privately held and family-linked. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Azelis is a Belgian-headquartered global distributor of specialty chemicals and food ingredients, supplying raw materials to makers of personal care, coatings, pharmaceuticals, food and industrial products. It operates in over 60 countries with revenue above 4 billion euros and has grown through acquisition. Based in Antwerp, Belgium, and listed on Euronext Brussels (AZE) since 2021, with private equity backer EQT historically involved. B2B intermediary with no consumer brand awareness.

Brookdale Senior Living is the largest US operator of senior living communities, based in Brentwood, Tennessee, running independent living, assisted living, memory care and continuing care retirement communities in about 40 states. It serves older adults and their families and earns revenue from resident fees. Listed on the NYSE (BKD), with roughly 650 communities and annual revenue near 3 billion dollars. Known to older consumers in the US; not a typical sports sponsor.

Clariant is a Swiss specialty chemicals company based in Muttenz near Basel, with products for catalysts, adsorbents, additives and care chemicals, sold to makers of plastics, oil and gas, mining, personal care and agriculture. It operates in around 90 countries with revenue near 4 billion Swiss francs and is listed on SIX Swiss Exchange (CLN), with Saudi SABIC a major shareholder. Spun out of Sandoz in 1995. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

DoubleVerify is a US digital media measurement and analytics software company that verifies ad quality for brand safety, fraud prevention, viewability and suitability. Advertisers, agencies and ad platforms use its tools to track whether adverts appear in safe, real environments, earning revenue from usage-based fees. Founded in 2008 in New York and listed on the NYSE (DV) since 2021, with revenue around 700 million dollars. B2B adtech with strong awareness among marketers and little among the public.

Ecovyst is a US specialty chemicals company, formerly PQ Group Holdings, based in Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. It makes silica catalysts and materials, zeolites and sulphuric acid regeneration services, selling to refiners, chemical makers, consumer goods and industrial customers. Listed on the NYSE (ECVT) with revenue around 700 million dollars. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Element Solutions is a US specialty chemicals company based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, formed from Platform Specialty Products. It supplies electronics chemistry for circuit boards, semiconductor packaging and assembly, plus industrial and specialty finishing chemistry. Customers are electronics, automotive and industrial manufacturers worldwide. Listed on the NYSE (ESI) with revenue near 2.4 billion dollars. B2B supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance is a Geneva-based public-private partnership launched in 2000 that funds vaccines for children in low-income countries. It pools donations from governments, the Gates Foundation and others to buy vaccines for diseases such as measles, polio, HPV and COVID-19 (through COVAX), and has helped vaccinate hundreds of millions of children. It is a non-profit international organisation, not a company. Strong profile in global health and development, but not a typical commercial sponsorship target.

Harry's is a US direct-to-consumer grooming and personal care company founded in 2013 in New York, known for razors and shaving products sold online and in retailers such as Target and Walmart. It also owns Flamingo, a women's body-care and shaving brand, and acquired Feldmühle razor factory in Germany. It earns revenue from razor, blade, shave gel and body product sales; an attempted sale to Edgewell was blocked in 2020. Consumer brand with strong US awareness and marketing spend.

Hithium Energy Storage is a Chinese battery maker founded in 2019 and based in Xiamen, Fujian, focused on lithium-ion cells and energy storage systems for utilities, solar and wind developers and commercial users. It produces large-format LFP cells, notably its 300Ah and 1175Ah cells, and sells containerised storage systems worldwide. It has raised significant venture and strategic funding and filed for a Hong Kong listing. B2B supplier with limited public brand awareness.

Ingram Micro is one of the world's largest technology distributors and service providers, supplying IT hardware, software, cloud, cybersecurity and logistics services to resellers and managed service providers in over 50 countries. Founded in 1979 and based in Irvine, California, it was owned by the Chinese conglomerate HNA and then Platinum Equity (2021) before returning to the NYSE (INGM) in 2024. Revenue is above 45 billion dollars. B2B distributor with brand awareness in the IT trade, but not among consumers.

International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF) is a US-headquartered maker of flavours, fragrances, food ingredients, health and biosciences ingredients and pharma solutions. It sells to makers of food and drinks, perfumes, household and personal care products, and has plants and labs worldwide. Based in New York, it was formed by IFF's 2021 merger with DuPont's nutrition and biosciences unit. Listed on the NYSE (IFF) with revenue near 11 billion dollars. B2B ingredient supplier with low consumer awareness.

MIS is a Saudi Arabian IT solutions and services company based in Riyadh, providing a full range of IT services including infrastructure, software, systems integration, managed services and support aligned with global standards. Customers are Saudi government entities and large enterprises. The input gives limited detail on size or ownership. B2B IT provider with limited public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Quest Global is a Singapore-headquartered engineering services company founded in 2003 in India, providing product design, development and manufacturing engineering for aerospace, automotive, rail, energy, medical devices, semiconductors and industrial clients. It has over 20,000 engineers across dozens of centres worldwide. Private, with investors including Bain Capital and Advent International. B2B engineering services provider with modest public awareness but credibility in aerospace and mobility.

Remy Cointreau is a French premium spirits group based in Paris, owning cognac Remy Martin and Louis XIII, the orange liqueur Cointreau, Metaxa, The Botanist gin, Bruichladdich and other whisky brands. It sells to consumers via distributors, with big exposure to China and the US, and revenue near 1 billion euros. Founded in 1724 as Remy Martin, it is listed on Euronext Paris (RCO). High-visibility luxury drinks brands, active in hospitality and sports sponsorship.

System1 is a US marketing technology and omnichannel customer acquisition company based in Marina Del Rey, California. Its platform uses data and responsive acquisition marketing to connect consumers to search, content and advertising from partners, and it owns brands such as Startpage and MapQuest. It went public through a 2022 SPAC merger with Trebia, and is listed on the NYSE (SST). Low direct public awareness, though its products reach many internet users.

The New York Times Company is a US news publisher headquartered in New York, producing The New York Times, plus The Athletic, Wirecutter, Cooking and the Games (Wordle) brands. Revenue is mostly from digital and print subscriptions (over 11 million subscribers) plus advertising, with annual revenue around 2.6 billion dollars. Founded in 1851, it is listed on the NYSE (NYT) and controlled by the Ochs-Sulzberger family. Globally recognised news brand with an affluent, educated audience, and The Athletic gives it sports reach.

Tipalti is a US-founded, Israel-rooted finance automation company based in Foster City, California, offering a platform for accounts payable, global supplier and partner payouts, tax compliance and reconciliation. Customers are mid-sized and large businesses, including marketplaces and technology firms, paying in many currencies and countries. It has raised funding at a valuation of around 8 billion dollars in 2021 from investors including Zeev Ventures, Greenoaks and Sequoia. B2B fintech with brand awareness among finance teams.

Unit4 is a Dutch enterprise software company headquartered in Utrecht, selling cloud ERP and financial management applications focused on people-centric sectors such as professional services, education, the public sector, non-profits and real estate. It has roughly 4,000 employees and serves customers in many countries. Founded in 1980 and owned by private equity Advent International since 2021, previously TA Associates. B2B software vendor with limited consumer awareness.

Aura Holdings is an Australian property developer based in Coorparoo, Brisbane, and is known for Aura City on the Sunshine Coast, a large master-planned community in the Caloundra South area. It provides luxury real estate development, and sells residential land and homes. It is private and its scale is the project size more than staff. Regional developer, with brand awareness in Queensland.

Clarios is a global maker of automotive batteries, headquartered in Glendale, Wisconsin (Milwaukee area), spun out of Johnson Controls in 2019 and owned by Brookfield Business Partners. It supplies roughly one in three of the world's cars with 12-volt and start-stop batteries, and sells the brands Varta, Optima, LTH and Interstate under OEM supply deals. It operates dozens of plants worldwide and has revenue near 9 billion dollars. Brands like Varta and Optima are visible to aftermarket consumers.

CPV Generation Holdings is the holding entity for a portfolio of natural gas power plants owned by Competitive Power Ventures, a US developer and operator of power generation and renewable energy projects. The input describes it as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary and shows limited details. It earns revenue from selling electricity and capacity into US wholesale markets. B2B power producer with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Liberty Broadband is a US holding company, based in Englewood, Colorado, whose main assets are a stake of about 30% in Charter Communications (Spectrum cable, internet and mobile) and the GCI Liberty Alaska operator GCI. It is controlled by John Malone's Liberty group and is listed on Nasdaq (LBRDA/LBRDK). Revenue comes from GCI's Alaska communications business. A financial holding vehicle with no consumer brand of its own, though GCI is well known in Alaska.

LiveOak Fiber is a US fiber broadband provider based in Brunswick, Georgia, building and operating fibre-to-the-home networks for residential and business customers in southeastern states. It is a privately held internet service provider backed by investors. The input only supports the sector and location, so scale is unknown. Local consumer-facing telecom brand with regional awareness only. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Navios Maritime Partners is a Greece-linked international shipping company, a publicly traded master limited partnership (NYSE: NMM) that owns and charters a large fleet of dry bulk vessels, containerships and tankers. Controlled by Angeliki Frangou's Navios group, it is based in Piraeus, Greece (with a Monaco address) and operates about 150 vessels on charters to commodity traders, container lines and oil companies. B2B shipping owner with no consumer brand profile.

Regional Link Telecom Services is a Hong Kong-based telecom and digital infrastructure business providing connectivity and related services. Crunchbase classes it under digital media and infrastructure. The input provides little more about its customers or scale. B2B provider with limited public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

T-Mobile Wren House JV is a 50/50 joint venture between T-Mobile US and Wren House Infrastructure Management, the infrastructure investor owned by the Kuwait Investment Authority. Formed in 2022, it acquired and runs a network of cell towers and related assets, with T-Mobile leasing capacity. It is a financing and asset vehicle rather than an operating consumer business, so it has no brand profile for sponsorship. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Andmore is a US company based in Las Vegas, Nevada, that, per Crunchbase, provides physical marketplaces and permanent retail spaces, a rental business model for brands and vendors. The input supports the sector and location, and little else, so scale and ownership are unknown. Consumer-facing in a local sense, with limited national brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

B Communications was an Israeli holding company listed on Nasdaq and the Tel Aviv exchange (BCOM) whose main asset was a controlling stake in Bezeq, Israel's largest telecom group. Controlled by Shaul Elovitch's Eurocom Group, it was a parent entity with no operating business of its own and was delisted and absorbed after Eurocom's corporate unwinding, around 2019 to 2021. Based in Tel Aviv. A financial holding vehicle with no brand profile of its own.

Cabify is a Spanish ride-hailing and mobility company founded in 2011 in Madrid, offering app-based taxi and private car services mainly in Spain and Latin America (Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Peru, Argentina and others). Customers are consumers and corporate travel accounts. Backed by investors including Rakuten, Santander and Korea's Mirae, with a valuation of about 1.4 billion dollars at peak. Recognisable consumer app in Spanish-speaking markets, with experience in sports sponsorship such as football.

Ceske Drahy (Czech Railways, CD) is the Czech Republic's national railway passenger operator, based in Prague, running domestic and international passenger trains, with the freight business, CD Cargo, now separated. It carries well over 150 million passengers a year and is wholly owned by the Czech state, competing with private operators such as RegioJet. High consumer visibility in the Czech Republic.

Conterra Broadband Services is a US fibre network company, based in Charlotte, North Carolina, that designs, builds and operates fibre and wireless backhaul infrastructure for wireless carriers, enterprises, schools and rural communities. It works largely in underserved areas of the Southeast and Midwest, earning revenue from wholesale and enterprise connectivity. Owned by Cartesian Capital Group (private equity). B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

The Hillman Group (Hillman Solutions) is a US distributor and maker of hardware and home improvement products such as fasteners, keys, key cutting kiosks, picture hanging, hooks, signs and engraving, sold through retailers including Home Depot, Lowe's and Walmart. It is based in Cincinnati, Ohio and went public through a 2021 SPAC merger with Landcadia IV (Nasdaq: HLMN). Revenue is about 1.5 billion dollars. B2B supplier with low consumer brand awareness, though the product is seen in stores.

KORE Wireless is a US Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity and solutions provider, based in Atlanta, Georgia, offering cellular IoT connectivity management, devices, fleet tracking and analytics to enterprises, healthcare, transportation and industrial customers. It went public in 2021 through a SPAC merger with Cerberus Telecom Acquisition Corp (NYSE: KORE) and has over 18 million connections. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

Madison Square Garden Entertainment is a US live entertainment company based in New York, spun off in 2023 from the former MSG Entertainment (now Sphere Entertainment). It owns and operates Madison Square Garden arena, Radio City Music Hall, The Theater at MSG, Chicago Theatre and the Hulu Theater, and manages the Tao Group Hospitality businesses. Revenue comes from ticketing, events, suites, sponsorship and food and drinks. Listed on the NYSE (MSGE). Very strong brand and an active partner for sponsorship.

October is a French fintech online lending platform founded in 2014 in Paris under the name Lendix, connecting small and medium-sized businesses seeking loans with institutional and retail investors in France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands. EROAD is a New Zealand telematics company based in Auckland, providing electronic road user charging, fleet management, compliance and safety technology for trucking and fleets in New Zealand, Australia and North America. It is listed on the NZX and ASX (ERD). B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Laiyifen is a Chinese snack and specialty food retailer based in Shanghai, selling snacks, nuts, baked goods and gifts through its stores and e-commerce platforms, including its app. Founded in 1998, it is listed in Shanghai and has a large chain of outlets in China. Consumer brand with strong awareness in China.

LightInTheBox is a Chinese online retailer, originally based in Beijing, selling apparel, home goods, small accessories and party dresses to consumers worldwide, with major markets in Europe and North America. Listed on the NYSE (LITB) since 2013. Cross-border e-commerce brand with moderate awareness among online shoppers.

OverActive Media Group is a Canadian esports and entertainment company based in Toronto that owns the Toronto Ultra (Call of Duty), the Toronto Defiant (Overwatch) and the MAD Lions KOI team in Spain, plus Esports Entertainment and the Rogers Place tie-ups. It is listed on the TSX (OAM). Sponsorship revenue is a key income source. Esports brand with real fan reach and active sponsorship partnerships.

SALTO Systems is a Spanish maker of electronic access control and smart locks, based in Oiartzun, Gipuzkoa, serving hotels, offices, universities, hospitals and residential buildings with cloud-based and wireless door locking systems. Founded in 2001, it sells in many countries through partners. Privately held. B2B brand known among hoteliers and integrators, not consumers.

Sow Good is a US maker of freeze-dried candy and snacks, based in Irving, Texas, selling products such as freeze-dried Sour Strawberry gummies under the Sow Good brand through retailers such as Walmart, Target and Kroger. It is listed on Nasdaq (SOWG). A fast-growing consumer snack brand, with a social media following.

Wheels India is an Indian maker of steel wheels for commercial vehicles, tractors, passenger cars and construction equipment, based in Chennai and part of the TVS group. It supplies automakers such as Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland and Mahindra and also exports. Listed on the NSE and BSE. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Alamar Foods is a Saudi food company based in Riyadh, the master franchisee of Domino's Pizza across the Middle East and North Africa, operating and franchising hundreds of Domino's stores in markets such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt and Jordan. It is part of the Alamar group and listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). Consumer-facing through the Domino's brand with strong regional awareness.

Burlington Stores is a US off-price retailer of apparel, shoes, home goods and accessories, formerly Burlington Coat Factory, headquartered in Burlington, New Jersey. It operates over 1,000 stores in the US and Puerto Rico, selling branded goods at discounted prices, with annual sales near 10 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (BURL). Strong consumer brand across the US, particularly among value-seeking shoppers.

ECTEK is a Chinese electric vehicle or automotive components company based in Changzhou, with listed status and funding of about 219 million yuan per the input. Its products and customers are not detailed. B2B with limited consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

EShallGo is a Chinese company based in Shanghai, listed on Nasdaq (EHGO), in e-commerce and leasing, operating a platform for IT hardware leasing and recycling aimed at small businesses, and for second-hand electronics. It has raised about 28 million dollars. B2B service with limited public brand awareness.

Motorcar Parts of America is a US maker and remanufacturer of automotive aftermarket parts, based in Torrance, California, including alternators, starters, wheel hubs, brake parts and turbochargers. It sells to auto parts retailers such as AutoZone, O'Reilly and Advance Auto Parts, with factories in Mexico, Malaysia and China. Listed on Nasdaq (MPAA). B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

RailVision is an Israeli technology company based in Ra'anana that makes long-range electro-optical sensor systems with AI to help trains detect obstacles and avoid collisions, selling to railway operators and rail vehicle makers. Listed on Nasdaq (RVSN) since 2022. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Shuangying Group is a Chinese automotive components manufacturer based in Liuzhou, Guangxi. The input shows listed status and funding of about 244 million yuan. Its products and customers are not detailed. B2B with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Society Pass is a Southeast Asian loyalty and e-commerce ecosystem company, with its head office in Singapore and operations in Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand, running consumer loyalty, ride-hailing, food delivery and advertising businesses. Listed on Nasdaq (SOPA) since 2021. Consumer-facing brands with regional presence and limited global awareness.

Wunong Net Technology is a Chinese online food retailer, based in Shenzhen, selling agricultural products and fresh food to consumers and businesses through its e-commerce platform and has been listed on Nasdaq (WNW) since 2020. It is a small business with funding of about 30 million dollars and limited brand awareness outside its local market.

YY Group Holding is a Singapore-based live streaming agency and hospitality-freelance services company, working with hosts and talent on platforms such as BIGO Live in Asia, and also offering freelance staffing. Listed on Nasdaq (YYGH) since 2024. B2B and creator economy business with small public brand awareness.

Advantage Solutions is a US sales and marketing services company, based in Irvine, California (the input lists St Louis), providing outsourced sales, merchandising, retail services and experiential marketing to consumer goods makers and retailers. It listed on Nasdaq (ADV) in 2020 through a SPAC merger and has about 70,000 staff. B2B with strong awareness among CPG brands and low among consumers.

Block.one is a blockchain software company, incorporated in the Cayman Islands (the input lists George Town) and led by Brendan Blumer, best known for creating the EOSIO software and raising about 4 billion dollars in the 2017-2018 EOS token sale. It has since invested in crypto ventures including Bullish exchange and the Voice platform. Privately held. Crypto-industry brand with little mainstream awareness.
